name: Architecture Decision Records
description: Record architecture decisions in ADR format to preserve context for future developers and your future self.
content:
# Architecture Decision Records Rules

- Create an ADR for every significant architecture decision — framework choices, database selection, API design patterns, deployment strategies
- Use a numbered filename format — `001-use-postgresql.md`, `002-adopt-event-sourcing.md` for chronological ordering
- Follow the standard ADR structure — Title, Status (proposed/accepted/deprecated/superseded), Context, Decision, Consequences
- Write the Context section to explain the problem — what forces or constraints led to needing this decision
- Write the Decision section in active voice — "We will use PostgreSQL" not "PostgreSQL was chosen"
- List both positive and negative Consequences — every decision has tradeoffs, document them honestly
- Keep ADRs immutable once accepted — if a decision changes, create a new ADR that supersedes the old one
- Link superseding ADRs — "Supersedes ADR-003" and update the old ADR's status to "Superseded by ADR-007"
- Store ADRs in the repository — `docs/decisions/` or `docs/adr/` so they travel with the code
- Don't create ADRs for trivial decisions — focus on choices that affect the system's structure, cost, or development approach
- Review ADRs during onboarding — they are the fastest way for new developers to understand why things are the way they are
- Include the date and participants — future readers need to know when the decision was made and who was involved
